small_guidance:
- The conv now dominates (~6.7ms baseline, kernel runs at 12.9ms — the fused pool/lse/relu is fine but Conv3d via cuDNN is the bottleneck). Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps on the existing pool kernel will not close the gap; only minor wins available (try BLOCK_S=128, num_warps=4, num_stages=2).
- Consider fusing the conv bias add into the producer or doing the pool directly on conv output without materializing — but the real headroom is replacing Conv3d.
- Ensure output tensor is contiguous and use `.contiguous()` on conv output if memory format mismatch causes strided loads.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`, with implicit im2col gather inside the kernel. Shapes are (4, 64, 32, 128, 128) with kernel 3³ and IC=32 — GEMM-K = 32*27 = 864, GEMM-M = 64, GEMM-N = up to 32*128*128. This is the dominant cost and has high headroom.
- Fuse conv bias + 2× MaxPool3d + channel logsumexp + ReLU into a single mega-kernel: each program computes a 2×2×2 pool window's conv outputs for all OC, takes max over the window, then LSE-reduces across OC, then ReLU, writing one scalar per output spatial position. This eliminates the intermediate (4,64,32,128,128)=128MB conv tensor entirely (huge bandwidth savings).
- Alternatively, keep conv separate but use a persistent GEMM with channels-last layout so the pool kernel reads contiguously along C. Autotune BLOCK_M/N/K over {32,64,128} × {32,64,128} × {32,64}.
